objective: Prepare a canonical release-signing ceremony manifest and verify witness, signer, threshold, transparency, trusted-root, phase, and replay evidence without creating a signature or claiming that an operator ceremony occurred.

research_inputs.finding: NIST SP 800-57 covers keying-material protection, key-management functions, key inventory, key recovery, compromise, digital signatures, split knowledge, trust anchors, and usage periods.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL separates witness and operator rosters, binds key IDs and trusted roots to the manifest, enforces thresholds, expiry, replay protection, and explicit authority boundaries.

research_inputs.finding: TUF root metadata identifies authorized keys and role thresholds; root key replacement/revocation changes root metadata, while snapshot and timestamp metadata bind versions and freshness.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL models a role, key roster, threshold, trusted-root ID, manifest digest, ordered phases, and transparency references.

research_inputs.finding: Sigstore binds identity to an artifact signature and records signing events in a timestamped transparency log; verification compares the signature, certificate/key, artifact, and transparency record under a trusted root.
research_inputs.implementation_impact: FAISAL requires signer key IDs, signature digests, transparency-log entries, trusted-root IDs, and verification references, while keeping cryptographic verification false until real evidence is supplied.

features: canonical release-tag, full-head, artifact, role, key-roster, operator-roster, witness-roster, threshold, and trusted-root manifest binding
monotonic event sequence and nonce replay protection
local preparation versus external-reference origin separation
signature and transparency evidence fields without local cryptographic assertion
production_approval, operator_ceremony_completed, signature_cryptographically_verified, and transparency_log_verified remain false

benchmark.scope: local Python ceremony-control-plane overhead; excludes real cryptographic signing, key custody, operator identity authentication, transparency-log contact, and production approval

limitations: All external-reference events in the validation fixture are synthetic structural fixtures and are not real operator signatures, witnesses, transparency records, or external verification.
The contract does not access private keys, HSMs, KMS, Sigstore/Fulcio/Rekor, TUF roots, or operator identity providers.
The contract records evidence references but does not cryptographically verify signatures or transparency-log inclusion.
The contract never marks an operator ceremony complete and never issues production approval.

rollback.rollback_scope: remove the signing-ceremony module, tests, benchmark, runner, evidence registration, and metadata; retain the qualification-intake release tag
